## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

# fo-intel

Family office intelligence: a pipeline that discovers family offices from public
sources and proves what each one is, and a product that makes the result
queryable in plain English.

**Live system:** https://fo-intel-web.vercel.app

Built for the PolarityIQ Differentiator. **Stage 2 is the current state**; see
[`docs/ACCEPTANCE_M3.md`](docs/ACCEPTANCE_M3.md) for the requirement-to-evidence
matrix and the deliverable index, and [`SUBMISSION.md`](SUBMISSION.md) for the
Stage 1 one, kept as history.

| surface | what it is |
|---|---|
| [`/`](https://fo-intel-web.vercel.app/) | plain-English search over the original Stage 1 corpus of 50 records |
| [`/shortlist`](https://fo-intel-web.vercel.app/shortlist) | the Stage 2 retrieval extension — filters, evidence grading, pagination over all 581 records |
| [`/agent`](https://fo-intel-web.vercel.app/agent) | the agent, using retrieval as a tool |
| [`/operations`](https://fo-intel-web.vercel.app/operations) | what ran, what it refused, and why |

Stage 2 documents: [architecture notes](docs/ARCHITECTURE_NOTES.md) ·
[inclusion standard](docs/INCLUSION_RUBRIC.md) ·
[build summary](docs/BUILD_SESSION_SUMMARY.md) ·
[AI working-session record](docs/ai-session/) ·
[exports](exports/)

---

## What it does

The pipeline finds candidate firms across four independent source classes, proves
what each firm actually is, enriches the ones that qualify, and writes records
where **every value carries its basis** — the exact evidence span it was read
from, the URL and tier of that source, the content hash at the time, and the
outcome of six validation gates under a named policy version. Stage 1 delivered
50 such records; Stage 2 operates the same contract at scale, unattended, on a

| contacts counting toward reachability without ownership evidence | **0** |
| released claims where `attribution` did not pass | **0** |

That last row is the one worth dwelling on. **1,307 claims are released and not
one** reached that state without the attribution gate explicitly passing. In
Stage 1, 93 of 155 quote-backed values were mis-wired. The defect class is now
structurally absent rather than merely unobserved.

### PTC-2, demonstrated and then discharged

Before the fix, 49 SEC `country` claims sat in `candidate`. Their evidence cited a
filing accession number, which the attribution gate classifies as *pointer*
evidence; pointer resolution is Band B and not built, so the gate returned
`skipped` and the release gate treated skipped as not-proven and **held** them.

That is the contract working as specified — an unchecked value did not reach a
customer wearing the appearance of a checked one. It was also the direct cause of
Blocker 1, and it is why the fix changed the *kind* of evidence rather than
loosening the gate. Held claims are now 0.

| gate | passed | failed | skipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| schema | 1315 | 0 | 0 |
| attribution | 1309 | 6 | 0 |
| value_type | 360 | 2 | 953 |
| coherence | 542 | 0 | 773 |
| contact_ownership | 40 | 1 | 1274 |
| identity | 0 | 0 | 1315 |

## 4. Operational behaviour

**Workflows.** Three, all `state=active` on default branch `main`, public repo,
valid cron. `discover` 02/08/14/20 UTC, `refresh` 05/17 UTC, `contract` on
`workflow_run` completion of either.

**Chaining proven.** GitHub's API records the `contract` run as
`event=workflow_run` — nothing human started it. The upstream `discover` shows
`event=workflow_dispatch`.

**Checkpoints advance and resume.** Three rows, keyed `(job, source_id)`:

| job | source | cursor | units |
|---|---|---|---|
| discover | companies_house | 13916919 | 60 |
| discover | sec_13f | name:ONEASCENT FAMILY OFFICE | 8 |
| refresh | companies_house | 13692510 | 40 |

Resume verified three times, including under real failure. The Companies House
cursor was written by the GitHub-hosted run, not locally. The `refresh` cursor was
written by the **scheduled** run. And when the SEC re-derivation was killed by a
10-minute command timeout at unit 41 of 49, the next invocation resumed at
`0001345471` and completed the remaining 8 units with no reprocessing and no
duplicates — the checkpoint doing exactly the job it exists for, against an
unplanned kill rather than a rehearsed one.

**Idempotency.** Deterministic entity ids; a content-hash short circuit that
writes nothing when a source is unchanged (observed: 9 of 9 unchanged on the
refresh run); checkpoints written only after the unit's writes commit.

**Logging.** Structured JSON to stdout (Actions log) and to `s2_run_log` in Neon,
because Actions logs expire and are not queryable. 176 rows across 12 runs, plus
124 rows in `s2_decision_log` (`classify` 118, `budget_halt` 3, `quarantine` 3).

**`/operations`** renders runs, gate outcomes, decisions, refused values and both
reachability metrics, all matching the database.

---

## 5. Blockers — both resolved

Only two were ever found. Everything else above is either met or later-phase work.

### Blocker 1 — RESOLVED 30 Jul 19:30 UTC

**Was:** zero records both qualifying and reachable. **Now: 39.**

| source | entities | qualifying | reachable | **both** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| companies_house | 69 | 65 | 0 | **0** |
| sec_13f | 49 | 46 | 40 | **39** |

Fixed inside the existing SEC extractor using `COVERPAGE.tsv` fields that were
already loaded — `FILINGMANAGER_STREET1`, `CITY`, `STATEORCOUNTRY`, `ZIPCODE`. No
new source, collector, architecture or policy.

The substantive change was to the *kind* of evidence, not the value. `country`
had been asserted from "Form 13F implies a US manager", citing the accession
number — pointer evidence, which gate 2 correctly deferred and the release gate
correctly held. Now the state code is read from the filing and the country is
re-derived from it by the already-registered `us_state_to_country` rule, so the
gate can check the claim instead of deferring it. All 49 previously-held claims
are now released, each with a detail line of the form *re-derived "United States"
from a two-letter US state code "NY" present in the span*.

The SEC entities were **re-derived, not patched** — their claims were dropped and
rebuilt from the observations, per the roadmap's rule for re-qualification.

**One entity is reachable but still withheld, correctly.** Long Focus Capital
Management files from San Juan, `PR`. The registered rule covers 50 states and
DC, so it returned null and the extractor declined to claim a country rather than
guess one. Whether US territories should map to "United States" is a policy
question, and policy was frozen. One-line fix available if wanted.

<details><summary>Original blocker text</summary>

| source | entities | qualifying | reachable | **both** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| companies_house | 69 | 65 | 0 | **0** |
| sec_13f | 49 | 0 | 40 | **0** |

The two populations are disjoint. Companies House publishes no contact routes;
SEC filers carry routes but fail the commercial floor, missing `country`,
`website` and `city`.

A record only counts toward the 500 if it qualifies, and only counts toward the
200 if it is reachable. **The intersection is currently 0**, so on this
trajectory both hard minimums fail regardless of how many records accumulate.

`country` is missing for a specific and fixable reason: the SEC extractor cites
the filing accession for it, which reads as pointer evidence and is correctly
held. The data to fix this is already loaded — `COVERPAGE.tsv` carries
`FILINGMANAGER_CITY`, `FILINGMANAGER_STATEORCOUNTRY`, `FILINGMANAGER_STREET1` and
`FILINGMANAGER_ZIPCODE` for every filer, and the `us_state_to_country` derivation
rule is already registered and tested.

Estimated fix: ~30 lines in the existing SEC extractor, no new architecture, no
new source. Expected effect: ~40 entities become qualifying **and** reachable.

*(Outcome: 39. Estimate was accurate.)*
</details>

The first scheduled run fired unattended:

```
refresh | event=schedule | completed/success | 2026-07-30T18:07:53Z
  -> contract | event=workflow_run | completed/success | 2026-07-30T18:16:33Z
```

GitHub's API attests both the `schedule` trigger and the chain. **The 48-hour
operating window opened at 30 Jul 18:07:53 UTC and closes 1 Aug 18:07 UTC**,
inside the submission deadline.

Note it fired at 18:07, not the configured 17:00. GitHub delays cron under load;
this is documented platform behaviour, not a fault, and is recorded here so the
timestamps in the logs are not read as a defect.

<details><summary>Original blocker text</summary>

All 8 runs to date are `trigger='manual'`. The 48-hour operating window is
measured from the first `schedule`-triggered run, and it has not started. Every
precondition is verified — workflows active, on the default branch, valid cron,
secrets present, a full manual execution green — but a future event cannot be
asserted, only observed.

Next opportunities: `refresh` 17:00 UTC, `discover` 20:00 UTC.

Until one fires, M3 cannot be signed off, the day-2 checkpoint email has nothing
to report, and the window cannot close inside the submission deadline.
</details>

---

## 6. Not blockers, but known and deliberate

- **`value_type` skips 761 of 1,123 claims.** Everything typed `string` has no
  registered checker, so `postcode`, `city` and date fields are unvalidated. A
  quality gap, not a correctness one — no false claim is produced, but a
  malformed one would not be caught.
- **`identity` skipped 1,123/1,123.** No profile claims exist yet; the gate has
  nothing to judge. It is proven against Stage 1's two wrong-person profiles in
  the test suite.
- **`contract` evaluates 0 claims** until `POLICY_VERSION` changes, by design. Its
  PTC-1 audit still runs every execution and fails the job on violation.
- **A `workflow_run`-triggered `contract` records as `trigger='manual'`,**
  understating unattended operation. It does not affect the window, which is
  measured from `discover`/`refresh`, and both record correctly.
- **The 13F dataset is a committed quarterly snapshot** (`data/sec/`, 2.9 MB).
  It will not pick up new filings until refreshed. Stated rather than implied.
- **A run killed by a command timeout left its row in `running`** during the
  re-derivation. `withRun` closes rows on normal failure but cannot on SIGKILL.
  It was closed as `aborted` with the reason recorded. Worth knowing because an
  Actions timeout would do the same, and a row stuck in `running` makes window
  queries ambiguous.
- **Puerto Rico is not in the derivation table**, so one reachable filer stays
  withheld. Correct refusal rather than a guess; see Blocker 1.


---

## The 500 requirement is unmet — measured, not estimated

**Frozen dataset:** 242 entities · **218 qualifying** · 67 strict reachable ·
174 profile-assisted · 47 postal · **187 with any defensible named-individual
route**.

The 500-record minimum is **not met**. This is a measured ceiling from every
channel built and every channel tested, not a shortfall of effort or runtime.
The qualification standard was never lowered to close it.

### Source ceilings, each measured

| channel | ceiling | how it was measured |
|---|---|---|
| Companies House | **exhausted** | narrow search returned 109 unique companies, **72% already held**, 31 new, 16 rejected as shells (never-filed, dormant, micro-entity), **15 net-new kept** |
| SEC 13F signatory | **56 filers** | full 2025Q3 census: 9,874 routes, 6,948 individually-owned across 6,944 filers, of which **exactly 56** carry `FAMILY`/`FAMILIES` in the registered name |
| SEC Form ADV | **27 net-new** | 942,258 filing rows scanned; 78 family-office-named registrants, 49 filed 2023+, **22 already held** via 13F |
| Verified profiles | **adds routes, not records** | 67% measured on a 30-entity sample; 107 routes created, zero new entities |
| Web discovery | **rejected at ~2–4% precision** | see below |
| **total measured ceiling** | **≈ 240** | against a requirement of 500 |

### The rejected web-discovery spike

40 Serper queries across the four exact phrases, 153 unique candidate domains, 45
fetched for first-party verification. 12 passed the automated filter (27%);
**1–2 were actually family offices**. True precision **~2–4%**.

What the filter let through: `privatebank.jpmorgan.com` and `bbh.com` (banks),
`daypitney.com` and `pillsburylaw.com` (law firms), `kaufmanrossin.com`
(accountancy), `sage.com` (accounting software), `kellogg.northwestern.edu` (a
university), `cowenpartners.com` (executive search), `uhnwinstitute.org` (a trade
body). Extracted "principals" were page furniture: *"Insights Reports Family"*,
*"Enterprise Value"*, *"Chief Investment Officer"*.

**The structural reason:** a single family office has no commercial reason to
publish a website. It serves one family and seeks no clients. The organisations
that rank for `"family office"` are precisely those *selling services to* family
offices, and no wording test separates "we are a family office" from "we advise
family offices".

Importing at that precision would have added ~150 records by placing banks and
law firms in a family-office dataset. The same call was made earlier against the
`family wealth` search terms, which returned independent financial advisers
(`IFS FAMILY WEALTH ADVISERS`, `REDWOOD FINANCIAL FAMILY WEALTH & ESTATE
PLANNERS`), and in Phase 0 against the leadership-page probe, which measured 0
of 26.

**Reproduce:** `WEB_QUERIES=40 WEB_FETCH=45 npx tsx packages/pipeline/src/discovery/sample-web.ts`

### The position, stated plainly

The brief says a submission below 500 fails, and also that a file containing
values labelled more strongly than the evidence supports cannot be trusted. Both
could not be satisfied from the sources available. **218 records that hold, with
the ceiling measurements attached, was chosen over 500 that do not.**


---

# Postscript — the 500 requirement, and how this section became wrong

Everything above this line was written when the file held 218 qualifying records
and I believed that was a measured ceiling. It is preserved unedited because it
was an honest reading of the evidence at the time and the correction is more
useful than a tidy document.

**The ceiling was a bug, not a limit.** Two defects in discovery, and the second
was the expensive one. Searches asked for `size=40` and never read the `hits`
total or used `start_index`, so a term with 286 matches returned 40. And the SIC
filter was an assumption about which codes family offices register under, not an
inclusion standard: `"family office"` filtered to SIC 64205 returns 11 hits;
unfiltered it returns 286. The firms behind that filter register under 68209,
70221, 68320 — whatever their accountant chose.

Fixing both took the qualifying count from 218 to 614 without relaxing a single
gate, the shell filter, the ownership adjudication or the commercial floor.

**Then two risk reviews took it back down.** The first, of the 27
records whose names suggested a service provider withheld ten: two insurers, two
family law firms, a tax practice, an IFA, two grantmaking foundations and a
consultancy. Seventeen ambiguous advisers and multi-family offices were retained
with their status unresolved, because the brief requires that ambiguity stay
visible rather than be cleaned away. That left 603.

**The second review, prompted by an external audit, found the deeper problem.**
The commercial floor asked whether a record was complete and never whether the
firm was a family office, so a bakery, a funeral home, a golf club, a
rail-supplies company, two acquisition shells and eleven hedge funds had
qualified on an address and a director alone — 54% of the file carried no
classification at all. Qualification now requires affirmative evidence at one of
three stated tiers and a named individual is mandatory. That cut the file to 554,
and further collection under the tightened standard brought it to **581**.

**Final state, reconciled across every surface:**

| | |
|---|---|

# Stage 2 — Technical Specification

Version 0.2 · **architecture draft, pending pre-build decisions** · owner: Muhammad Attique Ur Rehman

This is the specification we build from. It is not a description of what exists.
Anything here that turns out to be wrong gets amended here first, with the reason,
before the code changes.

---

## 0. What this system is

A family office intelligence platform whose product is **trustworthy claims**, not
answers. Every value a customer sees is a claim that survived a release gate, and
the evidence shown beside it is the evidence that established it.

Stage 1 promised that and did not deliver it. The measured failure: of 155
delivered values carrying a verbatim quote as evidence, **93 (60%) cite a quote
that does not contain or establish the value**. Root cause found at
`packages/pipeline/src/emit/build-dataset.ts:144` — a single line copying the
firm's *classification* evidence onto nine unrelated fields at assembly time.

That defect is the reason for most of the architecture below. The value was
correct; the binding between value and evidence was invented after the fact. The
fix is not a better validator. It is a data model in which that binding cannot be
created after the fact.

---

## 1. Architecture

### Deployables

| # | Deployable | Runs on | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `pipeline` | GitHub Actions (scheduled) | discovery, enrichment, validation, release, refresh |
| 2 | `web` | Vercel | customer product, retrieval, agent runtime |

Postgres (Neon) is the only thing they share. The pipeline writes; the web app
reads **released claims only** and has no write path to claim state.

### Why two, not ten

Collection → normalization → resolution → validation → release is a sequential
pipeline over one database. None of those stages scales independently, fails
independently in a useful way, or has a separate owner. Splitting them into
services would add nine network failure modes and a distributed release gate in
exchange for nothing at 500 records.

Boundaries are enforced as **modules with explicit interfaces**, so any stage can
be extracted later without redesign.

### Why the agent is not a third deployable

It needs the same released-claim reader and the same refusal boundary as
retrieval. A separate deployment adds a second thing that can be down when the
system is tested, and buys no isolation that matters — the authority boundary is
enforced in the tool interface, not by process separation.

### Module map

```
packages/
  core/          claim, evidence, source, status vocabulary, truth contract types
  db/            schema, migrations, released-claim reader, claim writer
  collect/       source adapters. one per source class. produce Observations only.
  extract/       Observation -> Claim + Evidence. the ONLY place evidence is created.
  resolve/        entity resolution, duplicate detection, cross-source conflict
  validate/      the gate battery. pure functions over claims. no I/O to sources.
  release/       the single chokepoint. claim trust + entity commercial state.
  refresh/       re-observation, decay detection, trust reduction
  contract/      Product Truth Contract as executable assertions
  agent/         tools, planner, authority boundary
apps/
  web/           product UI, retrieval API, agent route
```

---

## 2. Data model

### Principle

> A claim and the evidence that established it are produced by one act of reading
> one observation, share an immutable `extraction_event_id`, and are written in one
> transaction. Establishing evidence cannot be attached afterwards, by any code
> path.

This is the structural fix for the Stage 1 defect. `build-dataset.ts:144` was only
possible because evidence was a field you could assign. Here the binding is an
identity relationship the database can verify, not a convention the writer is
trusted to follow.

### Tables

**`source`** — a source *class* instance we can fetch from.
`id, kind, identifier, base_url, tier, rate_limit_per_min, last_ok_at, consecutive_failures`

`kind` ∈ `sec_submissions | sec_13f | sec_fulltext | companies_house | web_page | search_result`
`tier` ∈ `1 statutory/self | 2 press | 3 aggregator | 4 unranked` (carried from Stage 1, it worked)

**`observation`** — what a source returned, at a time. Immutable.
`id, source_id, url, fetched_at, content_hash, raw_ref, http_status, notes`

Raw bodies go to disk/object storage keyed by `content_hash`; the row holds the
pointer. Two fetches returning identical content share a hash — that is how decay
is detected in §7.

**`entity`** — a firm.
`id, canonical_name, entity_type, first_seen_at, merged_into_id, trust_state, commercial_state`

`trust_state` ∈ `active | merged | quarantined | retired`
`commercial_state` ∈ `qualifying | withheld | unassessed`

An entity enters customer retrieval only when `trust_state = active` **and**
`commercial_state = qualifying`. Splitting these is deliberate: a firm can be
entirely trustworthy and still too thin to sell, and the two failures need
different remedies — one needs better evidence, the other needs more enrichment.

**`claim`** — one assertion about one entity.
`id, entity_id, field, value_json, value_type, status, confidence, refresh_policy, established_at, expires_at, superseded_by_id`

`status` ∈ `candidate | validated | released | stale | quarantined | retired`

Note: there is no `withheld` claim status. Commercial sufficiency is judged on the
entity, not the claim — see §5.

**`extraction_event`** — one act of reading a source and deriving assertions.
`id, run_id, observation_id, extractor, started_at, ended_at`

Every claim and its establishing evidence are written inside one extraction event,
in one transaction. This is the identity relationship that makes the Stage 1
defect unexpressible — see PTC-10.

**`evidence`** — why we believe a claim.
`id, claim_id, observation_id, extraction_event_id, role, span_text, span_start, span_end, method, created_at`

`role` ∈ `establishing | corroborating | conflicting | superseding`

- **establishing** — the span the extractor actually read to derive this value.
  Exactly one per claim. Written in the claim's own extraction event. Never
  attachable afterwards.
- **corroborating** — an independent source later found to agree. May be attached
  after the fact, raises confidence, **cannot** promote status on its own.
- **conflicting** — an independent source that disagrees. Attaching one is a
  trust event and routes the claim to gate 7.
- **superseding** — a later observation that replaces the value. Creates a *new*
  claim in a new extraction event; the old claim is retired, not edited.

`span_text` is the exact text read. `method` is the human sentence shown to a
customer. There is **no generic attach-evidence API**: the writer takes a role and
refuses `establishing` outside an open extraction event.

**`validation_result`** — one row per gate per claim per run.
`id, claim_id, run_id, gate, outcome, detail, counterfactual`

`counterfactual` records what the claim *would have been* had the gate not fired.
That is what proves a validator is load-bearing rather than decorative.

**`release_decision`** — the audit trail of the chokepoint.
`id, claim_id, run_id, decision, gates_passed, gates_failed, policy_version, decided_at`

**`contact`** — specialised claim, because reachability is a hard bar.
`id, entity_id, person_claim_id, channel, value, reaches, ownership_evidence_id, verification_method, verified_at, status`

`reaches` ∈ `individual | team | company | unknown` — **never inferred, always evidenced**
`channel` ∈ `email | phone | linkedin | postal`

449	
450	## 0. What this system is
451	
452	A family office intelligence platform whose product is **trustworthy claims**, not
453	answers. Every value a customer sees is a claim that survived a release gate, and
454	the evidence shown beside it is the evidence that established it.
455	
456	Stage 1 promised that and did not deliver it. The measured failure: of 155
457	delivered values carrying a verbatim quote as evidence, **93 (60%) cite a quote
458	that does not contain or establish the value**. Root cause found at
459	`packages/pipeline/src/emit/build-dataset.ts:144` — a single line copying the
460	firm's *classification* evidence onto nine unrelated fields at assembly time.
461	
462	That defect is the reason for most of the architecture below. The value was
463	correct; the binding between value and evidence was invented after the fact. The
464	fix is not a better validator. It is a data model in which that binding cannot be
465	created after the fact.
466	
467	---
468	
469	## 1. Architecture
470	
471	### Deployables
472	
473	| # | Deployable | Runs on | Responsibility |
474	|---|---|---|---|
475	| 1 | `pipeline` | GitHub Actions (scheduled) | discovery, enrichment, validation, release, refresh |
476	| 2 | `web` | Vercel | customer product, retrieval, agent runtime |
477	
478	Postgres (Neon) is the only thing they share. The pipeline writes; the web app
479	reads **released claims only** and has no write path to claim state.
480	
481	### Why two, not ten
482	
483	Collection → normalization → resolution → validation → release is a sequential
484	pipeline over one database. None of those stages scales independently, fails
485	independently in a useful way, or has a separate owner. Splitting them into
486	services would add nine network failure modes and a distributed release gate in
487	exchange for nothing at 500 records.
488	
489	Boundaries are enforced as **modules with explicit interfaces**, so any stage can
490	be extracted later without redesign.
491	
492	### Why the agent is not a third deployable
493	
494	It needs the same released-claim reader and the same refusal boundary as
495	retrieval. A separate deployment adds a second thing that can be down when the
496	system is tested, and buys no isolation that matters — the authority boundary is
497	enforced in the tool interface, not by process separation.
498	
499	### Module map
500	
501	```
502	packages/
503	  core/          claim, evidence, source, status vocabulary, truth contract types
504	  db/            schema, migrations, released-claim reader, claim writer
505	  collect/       source adapters. one per source class. produce Observations only.
506	  extract/       Observation -> Claim + Evidence. the ONLY place evidence is created.
507	  resolve/        entity resolution, duplicate detection, cross-source conflict
508	  validate/      the gate battery. pure functions over claims. no I/O to sources.
509	  release/       the single chokepoint. claim trust + entity commercial state.
510	  refresh/       re-observation, decay detection, trust reduction
511	  contract/      Product Truth Contract as executable assertions
512	  agent/         tools, planner, authority boundary
513	apps/
514	  web/           product UI, retrieval API, agent route
515	```
516	
517	---
518	
519	## 2. Data model
520	
521	### Principle
522	
523	> A claim and the evidence that established it are produced by one act of reading
524	> one observation, share an immutable `extraction_event_id`, and are written in one
525	> transaction. Establishing evidence cannot be attached afterwards, by any code
526	> path.
527	
528	This is the structural fix for the Stage 1 defect. `build-dataset.ts:144` was only
529	possible because evidence was a field you could assign. Here the binding is an
530	identity relationship the database can verify, not a convention the writer is
531	trusted to follow.
532	
533	### Tables
534	
535	**`source`** — a source *class* instance we can fetch from.
536	`id, kind, identifier, base_url, tier, rate_limit_per_min, last_ok_at, consecutive_failures`
537	
538	`kind` ∈ `sec_submissions | sec_13f | sec_fulltext | companies_house | web_page | search_result`
539	`tier` ∈ `1 statutory/self | 2 press | 3 aggregator | 4 unranked` (carried from Stage 1, it worked)
540	
541	**`observation`** — what a source returned, at a time. Immutable.
542	`id, source_id, url, fetched_at, content_hash, raw_ref, http_status, notes`
543	
544	Raw bodies go to disk/object storage keyed by `content_hash`; the row holds the
545	pointer. Two fetches returning identical content share a hash — that is how decay
546	is detected in §7.
547	
548	**`entity`** — a firm.
549	`id, canonical_name, entity_type, first_seen_at, merged_into_id, trust_state, commercial_state`
550	
551	`trust_state` ∈ `active | merged | quarantined | retired`
552	`commercial_state` ∈ `qualifying | withheld | unassessed`
553	
554	An entity enters customer retrieval only when `trust_state = active` **and**
555	`commercial_state = qualifying`. Splitting these is deliberate: a firm can be
556	entirely trustworthy and still too thin to sell, and the two failures need
557	different remedies — one needs better evidence, the other needs more enrichment.
558	
559	**`claim`** — one assertion about one entity.
560	`id, entity_id, field, value_json, value_type, status, confidence, refresh_policy, established_at, expires_at, superseded_by_id`
561	
562	`status` ∈ `candidate | validated | released | stale | quarantined | retired`
563	
564	Note: there is no `withheld` claim status. Commercial sufficiency is judged on the
565	entity, not the claim — see §5.
566	
567	**`extraction_event`** — one act of reading a source and deriving assertions.
568	`id, run_id, observation_id, extractor, started_at, ended_at`
569	
570	Every claim and its establishing evidence are written inside one extraction event,
571	in one transaction. This is the identity relationship that makes the Stage 1
572	defect unexpressible — see PTC-10.
573	
574	**`evidence`** — why we believe a claim.
575	`id, claim_id, observation_id, extraction_event_id, role, span_text, span_start, span_end, method, created_at`
576	
577	`role` ∈ `establishing | corroborating | conflicting | superseding`
578	
579	- **establishing** — the span the extractor actually read to derive this value.
580	  Exactly one per claim. Written in the claim's own extraction event. Never
581	  attachable afterwards.
582	- **corroborating** — an independent source later found to agree. May be attached
583	  after the fact, raises confidence, **cannot** promote status on its own.
584	- **conflicting** — an independent source that disagrees. Attaching one is a
585	  trust event and routes the claim to gate 7.
586	- **superseding** — a later observation that replaces the value. Creates a *new*
587	  claim in a new extraction event; the old claim is retired, not edited.
588	
589	`span_text` is the exact text read. `method` is the human sentence shown to a
590	customer. There is **no generic attach-evidence API**: the writer takes a role and
591	refuses `establishing` outside an open extraction event.
592	
593	**`validation_result`** — one row per gate per claim per run.
594	`id, claim_id, run_id, gate, outcome, detail, counterfactual`
595	
596	`counterfactual` records what the claim *would have been* had the gate not fired.
597	That is what proves a validator is load-bearing rather than decorative.
598	
599	**`release_decision`** — the audit trail of the chokepoint.
600	`id, claim_id, run_id, decision, gates_passed, gates_failed, policy_version, decided_at`
601	
602	**`contact`** — specialised claim, because reachability is a hard bar.
603	`id, entity_id, person_claim_id, channel, value, reaches, ownership_evidence_id, verification_method, verified_at, status`
604	
605	`reaches` ∈ `individual | team | company | unknown` — **never inferred, always evidenced**
606	`channel` ∈ `email | phone | linkedin | postal`
607	
608	A contact counts toward the reachability bar only when `reaches = individual` and
609	`ownership_evidence_id` is non-null.
610	
611	**`signal`** — dated activity. Append-only, never re-verified.
612	`id, entity_id, kind, summary, occurred_at, evidence_id, source_tier`
613	
614	**`run`** — one scheduled execution.
615	`id, trigger, started_at, ended_at, job, records_touched, claims_created, claims_released, claims_quarantined, failures_json, cost_json, status`
616	
617	**`decision_log`** — every consequential decision, one row.
618	`id, run_id, entity_id, claim_id, kind, rule, before_json, after_json, reason, at`
619	
620	### Deferred
621	
622	`relationship` and `retrieval_document`. The first is real intelligence but no
623	Stage 2 requirement needs it. The second must be a **projection built at index
624	time from released claims**, never a stored table — a stored copy drifts from its
625	claims, and a drifted chunk enters retrieval, passes every downstream check, and
626	misleads the customer. That is exactly the failure mode Correction 7 describes.
627	
628	---
629	
630	## 3. Claim lifecycle
631	
632	```
633	                 extract
634	  observation ─────────────► candidate
635	                                 │
636	                          validate battery
637	                                 │
638	                    ┌────────────┴────────────┐
639	                    ▼                         ▼
640	               validated                 quarantined
641	                    │                    (evidence problem)
642	              release gate
643	                    │
644	                    ▼
645	                released ──── refresh cycle ────► stale ──► re-extract
646	                    │                                          │
647	                    └──────── superseded ◄─────────────────────┘
648	```
649	
650	**Rules**
651	
652	- A claim may only move to `released` through `release/gate.ts`. One function. All
653	  other write paths are compile-time prevented by not exporting a setter.
654	- **Trust is claim-level. Commercial sufficiency is record-level.** A claim that
655	  passes its trust gates is `released` and stays valid even if the record it
656	  belongs to is not yet commercially complete. `withheld` is therefore *not* a
657	  claim status — it is an **entity** state (§5).
658	- A superseded claim is retained, not deleted. Retraction history is product value
659	  and is required for the staleness evidence.
660	
661	---
662	
663	## 4. Validation pipeline
664	
665	Gates run in two bands.
666	
667	**Band A — cheap, deterministic (gates 1–6 where they need no network).** All of
668	them run, always, and every outcome is recorded even after one fails. Stopping at
669	the first failure saves compute and costs diagnosis: you fix one defect, re-run
670	500 records, and discover the second. At this volume the compute is trivial and
671	the round trip is not.
672	
673	**Band B — expensive or probabilistic (pointer resolution, conflict adjudication,
674	commercial scoring).** Skipped once Band A has already made release impossible,
675	and the skip is recorded as `skipped: release already blocked` rather than as a
676	pass. A gate that did not run never counts as a gate that passed — that is PTC-2.
677	
678	| # | Gate | Question | Catches (Stage 1 evidence) |
679	|---|---|---|---|
680	| 1 | `schema` | right shape, right type? | — |
681	| 2 | `attribution` | does the cited span contain or establish this value? | the 93 mis-wired values |
682	| 3 | `value_type` | does a person field hold a person? | 5 companies shipped as "Person with significant control" |
683	| 4 | `identity` | is this the entity we think, not a namesake? | 2 LinkedIn profiles belonging to different people |
684	| 5 | `contact_ownership` | does this route demonstrably reach the named individual? | 3 `info@` inboxes as principal email |
685	| 6 | `coherence` | is the record true as a whole, one source per composite? | Kopp address assembled from two filings |
686	| 7 | `conflict` | do sources disagree? which wins, at what confidence? | classification badge over a 3-way-described firm |
687	| 8 | `freshness` | is this within its refresh policy? | 25 records with no dated signal |
688	| 9 | `commercial` | does the record help decide whom to approach and why now? | no AUM/sector/thesis anywhere |
689	| 10 | `copy` | does every rendered sentence check its own precondition? | "reachable at the registered address above" on 10 cards with no address |
690	
691	**Gate 2 is the centrepiece.** It is the same lexical test Stage 1 applied to
692	generated answers, now pointed at the dataset — which is exactly what Correction 2
693	demands. Two evidence kinds are scored differently:
694	
695	- **quoting evidence** — the span must contain the value's hard tokens (numbers,
696	  dates, proper nouns) and reach 60% content-word coverage
697	- **pointer evidence** — the span names a record locator (company number, CIK,
698	  accession). Passes only if the locator resolves and the pointed-at record
699	  contains the value. Slower; runs asynchronously and downgrades on failure.
700	
701	**Gate 10 is unusual and deliberate.** Interface copy is data. Every fixed
702	sentence in the UI registers a precondition; the gate asserts the precondition is
703	checked before render. Correction 8 says user-visible sentences are held to the
704	same truth standard as values, and almost nothing in the industry tests this.
705	
706	---
707	
708	## 5. Release gate
709	
710	```ts
711	// release/gate.ts — the only path to released state
712	releaseDecision(claim, evidence, gateResults, policy) -> Decision
713	```
714	
715	**Two independent questions at two different levels**, per Correction 4:
716	
717	1. **Is this claim trustworthy?** Gates 1–8, per claim. Failure → claim
718	   `quarantined`, reason recorded. Passing claims are `released` and remain valid
719	   regardless of what the rest of the record looks like.
720	2. **Is this entity commercially sufficient?** Gate 9, per entity, over its
721	   released claims. Failure → `commercial_state = withheld`. The claims stay
722	   released and true; the entity does not enter customer retrieval and does not
723	   count toward the 500.
724	
725	The separation matters operationally: a withheld entity is a **work item for
726	enrichment**, not a data-quality problem. Conflating the two would send us hunting
727	for evidence defects in records whose only fault is thinness.
728	
729	A record is *counted toward the 500* only when it holds a released identity claim,
730	a released classification claim with function evidence (§9), and passes the
731	record-level commercial floor.
732	
733	**Policy is versioned data, not code.** `policy_version` on every decision. When
734	the standard tightens, previously released claims are re-evaluated on the next run
735	and can be demoted. This is what makes release a pipeline rather than a boolean.
736	
737	**Invariant:** no released claim exists without a `release_decision` row naming the
738	gates that ran. A claim in released state with no decision row is a bug that fails
739	the build.
740	
741	---
742	
743	## 6. Product Truth Contract — executable
744	
745	Not a document. A test suite that runs in CI and at release, and **fails the build**.
746	
747	`contract/rules.ts` exports one function per clause, each returning
748	`{ pass, violations[] }` over the released dataset and the rendered interface.
749	
750	| ID | Clause | Assertion |
751	|---|---|---|
752	| PTC-1 | No claim without evidence | every released claim has ≥1 evidence row passing gate 2 |
753	| PTC-2 | No status without a check | status vocabulary is closed; each status names the gate granting it; assert no claim carries a status whose gate never ran on it |
754	| PTC-3 | Contacts state who they reach | no contact labelled `individual` without `ownership_evidence_id` |
755	| PTC-4 | Labels match state | every rendered string has a registered precondition, checked before render |
756	| PTC-5 | Records coherent whole | gate 6 passed at record level, not only field level |
757	| PTC-6 | Counts are computed | every displayed number derives from released data at render time; no constants |
758	| PTC-7 | Absence ≠ failure | "looked, found nothing" and "could not look" are distinct states with distinct copy |
759	| PTC-8 | Refresh policy declared | every released claim names its policy and `expires_at` |
760	| PTC-9 | No label upgrade | a value's presented term is derived from its status, never chosen for tone |
761	| PTC-10 | Evidence is bound at extraction | every released claim has exactly one `establishing` evidence row sharing its `extraction_event_id`; no `establishing` row exists whose extraction event differs from its claim's |
762	
763	PTC-10 is the regression test for the Stage 1 defect, and it is an **identity**
764	invariant rather than a temporal one. An earlier draft asserted that evidence must
765	not be created after its claim, tested on timestamps. That was weak: clock skew,
766	batched inserts inside the same millisecond, and back-dated writes all defeat it,
767	and it does not actually prevent post-hoc attachment — it only makes some cases
768	detectable.
769	
770	Sharing an `extraction_event_id` is structural. The claim and the span that
771	established it were produced by one act of reading one observation, and the
772	database can prove it. Corroborating and conflicting evidence attach later by
773	design, carry a different role, and cannot promote a claim on their own.
774	
775	**The contract's pass rate is published in the product**, with failures visible.
776	The differentiator is not "we verify our data" — it is "here are ten assertions
777	our data must satisfy, here is today's score, here is what failed."
778	
779	---
780	
781	## 7. Scheduler and operating model
782	
783	**Platform: GitHub Actions.** Keeps its own run history, screenshot-able,
784	free, and the history is independently inspectable — which the brief requires.
785	
786	### Jobs
787	
788	| Job | Cadence | Does |
789	|---|---|---|
790	| `discover` | every 6h | climb toward 500: new candidates, extract, validate, release |
791	| `refresh` | every 12h, offset | re-observe released claims past `expires_at`, detect decay |
792	| `contract` | after each | run the PTC suite, write results, demote violators |
793	
794	**Concurrency and budget** — the brief scores this explicitly.
795	
796	- Per-run token budget, checked before each model call; run halts cleanly at 80%
797	  and records why rather than dying mid-record
798	- Per-source rate limits from the `source` table; a source returning 429 or 5xx
799	  three times consecutively opens a circuit breaker and is skipped for the run
800	- Work queue with bounded concurrency per source class (SEC 4, Companies House 2,
801	  web 8 — carried from Stage 1 where these were tuned against real limits)
802	- Every unit of work is idempotent and checkpointed: a run interrupted at record
803	  300 resumes at 300, and re-running a completed unit is a no-op
804	
805	### Staleness — evidence-based, not clock-based
806	
807	The brief is explicit that clock expiry alone does not satisfy the requirement.
808	Mechanism:
809	
810	1. `refresh` re-fetches the observation behind a released claim
811	2. Compares `content_hash` to the stored one
812	3. **Unchanged** → bump `last_reverified_at`, claim stays released
813	4. **Changed** → re-extract; if the value differs, the old claim is superseded and
814	   the new one enters validation; the decision log records *what changed*
815	5. **Source dark** (404/410/persistent 5xx) → trust reduced, claim → `stale`,
816	   reason `source no longer reachable at T`
817	6. **Contradiction** → claim → `quarantined`, both observations retained
818	
819	Only paths 4–6 count as the required staleness event, because only they carry an
820	evidence-based reason.
821	
822	---
823	
824	## 8. Agent decision boundaries
825	
826	### Tools
827	
828	| Tool | Reads | Cannot |
829	|---|---|---|
830	| `search_firms` | released claims only | see candidate, quarantined, withheld |
831	| `get_firm` | one entity's released claims + evidence | fabricate absent fields |
832	| `compare_firms` | released claims across entities | rank on a metric no claim holds |
833	| `check_evidence` | evidence + validation results | assert beyond the gate outcome |
834	| `count_matching` | released claims | estimate |
835	
836	Every tool returns `{ data, scope, excluded, limits }`. **Scope is mandatory** —
837	what was searched, what matched, what was excluded and why. That is how the agent
838	can state scope in its answer, which Correction 8 requires everywhere.
839	
840	### Authority
841	
842	**May decide alone:** how to decompose a goal, which tools and in what order, when
843	it has enough, how to structure output, when to stop.
844	
845	**Must abstain, with reason:** any claim not backed by released data; any ranking
846	where no claim holds the metric; any confidence assertion where evidence is thin
847	or conflicting; any contact characterisation beyond the `reaches` value.
848	
849	**Must refuse:** naming a firm not in the dataset, upgrading a label (company
850	inbox → principal email, one dated investment → standing mandate, "not found" →
851	"does not exist"), answering a narrower question than asked without saying so.
852	
853	That last one is the Stage 1 live failure: asked for principal-owned contact
854	routes excluding inboxes, the system answered "firms with any populated contact
855	field" and never said it had narrowed the question. **A constraint the system
856	cannot honour must be declined or explicitly narrowed in the answer, in plain
857	words.** This is enforced in control flow: the planner records the constraints it
858	could not honour, and the composer must surface them or the answer is blocked.
859	
860	### Deliberately not agentic
861	
862	Extraction, validation, release, and refresh are **fixed pipelines with no model
863	deciding control flow**. A model that can decide whether a claim is released can
864	decide to release a bad one. The model's role there is bounded extraction inside a
865	step whose output is mechanically checked. Architecture Note 2 asks what we kept
866	under fixed control and why — this is the answer.
867	
868	---
869	
870	## 9. Entity classification — function, not ownership
871	
872	Correction 3: family ownership proves control, not that the firm *operates* as a
873	family office.
874	
875	**Categories** — each requires affirmative evidence of the named kind:
876	
877	| Category | Requires |
878	|---|---|
879	| `single_family_office` | evidence of managing one family's wealth/investments as its purpose |
880	| `multi_family_office` | evidence of serving multiple unrelated families as clients |
881	| `family_holding_company` | family control evidenced, **no** evidence of wealth-management function |
882	| `adviser_or_wealth_manager` | excluded |
883	| `unconfirmed` | does not count |
884	
885	`family_holding_company` is a new category and exists because Stage 1's SFO-1 rule
886	(surname match + PSC + substance) proves exactly that and no more. Twenty of the
887	fifty qualified under it. Under this spec those records **do not count as family
888	offices** until function evidence is found — and the honest ones will be
889	reclassified rather than relabelled.
890	
891	**Function evidence** examples, in tier order: the firm describing its own purpose;
892	a statutory filing stating it manages family capital; a filing describing a pooled
893	vehicle for a single family (the Piton case in Stage 1 — the strongest evidence in
894	the whole file); credible press describing the function.
895	
896	---
897	
898	## 10. Logging
899	
900	Three streams, three purposes.
901	
902	**`run`** — one row per scheduled execution. Proves the operating window. Permanent.
903	
904	**`decision_log`** — every consequential decision with rule, before, after, reason.
905	Includes the counterfactual on rejection. **This is the log that earns credit**,
906	because a control earns credit when it changes what the system may do.
907	
908	**Agent trace** — per goal: action sequence, tool calls with arguments and returns,
909	intermediate decisions, retries, rejected paths, abstentions. JSON, raw,
910	submitted unedited for the three goals.
911	
912	Not logged: per-request debug noise. Raw enough to see what happened, quiet enough
913	that the signal is findable.
914	
915	---
916	
917	## 11. Evaluation
918	
919	Stage 1's suite measured the layer we were confident in. Stage 2 attacks the
920	surfaces where the live failures actually were.
921	
922	**Retained:** the 15 grounding cases, re-run against the deployed system after any
923	material change. Stage 1 shipped numbers from a system that no longer existed;
924	that does not repeat.
925	
926	**New case families, one per known failure class:**
927	
928	| Family | Probes |
929	|---|---|
930	| contact ownership | "email addresses that reach the named principal, not company inboxes" — must return only `reaches=individual` and state the count |
931	| evidence provenance | "show me the evidence for X's address" — the panel must prove the value above it |
932	| profile identity | LinkedIn/profile links belong to the named person |
933	| constraint preservation | a request with three constraints the system can only honour two of — must narrow explicitly |
934	| headline counts | every displayed number recomputes from the file |
935	| absence | ask for a firm not present — plain business answer, no machinery description |
936	| whole-record coherence | ask for the address of the record with the known assembly defect |
937	
938	**Rule:** a measured result must change what ships, or the notes must defend from
939	evidence why it did not.
940	
941	---
942	
943	## 12. UI architecture
944	
945	Not a chat box with cards. A workspace.
946	
947	**Search** → filters on commercially meaningful criteria (type, geography, mandate
948	signals, contact reachability, evidence grade, freshness), each stating why a
949	result matched.
950	
951	**Results** → sortable, comparable without opening each record. Trust grade and
952	freshness visible in the row, not buried.
953	
954	**Compare** → selected firms side by side, fields aligned, differences and gaps
955	explicit.
956	
957	**Record** → claims with status, evidence inspectable inline, contact routes
958	labelled with who they reach, signals dated, conflicts shown rather than resolved
959	silently.
960	
961	**Trust surface** → the PTC pass rate, what failed, what it means. This is the
962	product's differentiator made visible.
963	
964	**Absence and failure states** → business language, no machinery. "We hold no
965	mandate evidence for these firms; here is what we do hold" — not "the retrieval
966	returned no matching chunks."
967	
968	Every string registers a precondition (PTC-4). A sentence that can be false is a
969	defect of the same severity as a wrong value.
970	
971	---
972	
973	## 13. Failure handling
974	
975	| Failure | Response |
976	|---|---|
977	| source 429 / 5xx | exponential backoff; 3 consecutive → circuit breaker, skip for run, log |
978	| source blocks / 403 | mark source degraded, record in run log, continue with others |
979	| model malformed output | retry once; then fall back down the model chain; then abstain and record |
980	| model quota exhausted | remembered for 30 min, chain advances, run continues (Stage 1 lesson: both Llama models hit daily ceilings and the demo went dark) |
981	| entity unresolvable | quarantine, do not guess, replenish from discovery |
982	| run interrupted | checkpointed; resume from last committed unit; idempotent writes make re-run safe |
983	| DB unavailable | run fails fast and loudly rather than half-writing |
984	
985	**Induced failure**, if nothing breaks naturally: point a source adapter at a URL
986	that 403s, or feed the extractor a deliberately malformed page. Labelled as induced
987	in the log. The brief permits this and asks for honesty about it.
988	
989	---
990	
991	## 14. ADRs
992	
993	**ADR-1 · Two deployables, not ten services.**
994	The stages are a sequential pipeline over one database with no independent scaling
995	or failure domains. Services would add nine network failure modes and a distributed
996	release gate for no benefit at this scale. *Rejected:* microservices. *Cost:* one
997	process can exhaust another's resources; accepted because budget guards are
998	per-run.
999	
1000	**ADR-2 · Evidence is created only by extractors, bound to an observation span.**
1001	The Stage 1 defect was possible because evidence was an assignable field. Here
1002	there is no setter. *Cost:* extractors become the only place enrichment can add
1003	provenance; more code duplication across adapters. Accepted — the alternative is
1004	the bug that failed Stage 1.
1005	
1006	**ADR-3 · Claim and Fact are one table with a status.**
1007	Two tables means a sync problem and two sources of truth. *Rejected:* separate
1008	`fact` table.
1009	
1010	**ADR-4 · RetrievalDocument is a projection, never stored state.**
1011	A stored copy drifts from its claims; a drifted chunk passes every downstream
1012	check and misleads the customer. *Cost:* index rebuild on release. Cheap at 500.
1013	
1014	**ADR-5 · The release gate is one function.**
1015	Multiple write paths mean no gate. *Cost:* a bottleneck in code; irrelevant at this
1016	volume.
1017	
1018	**ADR-6 · Extraction, validation and release contain no agentic control flow.**
1019	A model that decides releases can release a bad claim. Models are used inside
1020	bounded steps whose output is mechanically checked. *Cost:* less adaptive; that is
1021	the point.
1022	
1023	**ADR-7 · Release policy is versioned data.**
1024	Lets a tightened standard demote already-released claims on the next run, which is
1025	what makes release a pipeline. *Cost:* re-evaluation cost per run.
1026	
1027	**ADR-8 · Staleness is evidence-based, via content hashing.**
1028	Clock expiry alone is explicitly insufficient. *Cost:* every refresh is a real
1029	fetch. This is the dominant cost driver — see §15.
1030	
1031	**ADR-9 · `family_holding_company` is a distinct category.**
1032	Stage 1's SFO-1 rule proved family control, not family-office function. Twenty
1033	records qualified on it. Splitting the category is honest reclassification rather
1034	than relabelling. *Cost:* the qualifying count drops before it rises.
1035	
1036	**ADR-12 · A statutory service address is a third reachability metric, never folded into the other two.**
1037	
1038	Companies House requires every director to file a service address: the address at
1039	which they personally accept legal documents. Adjudicated the same way SEC phone
1040	numbers are -- rejected if it is the registered office, if another company uses
1041	it, or if a second director at the firm shares it -- it survives at a rate of 206
1042	from 641 on the Stage 1 candidate file. The 435 rejections are the point: an
1043	unadjudicated count would be three times larger and mean nothing.
1044	
1045	On the brief's wording it qualifies. A route counts if it reaches the named
1046	individual, and the exclusions named are shared inboxes, contact forms,
1047	switchboards and pattern-generated addresses. An adjudicated service address is
1048	none of those, is filed by the individual, and is statutory tier-1 evidence.
1049	
1050	It is also **commercially weaker than a phone or a personal email**, and a
1051	reviewer recomputing our reachable count would be within their rights to say a
1052	postal address is not a usable route for a fund manager seeking LPs. That
1053	disagreement is legitimate, and the number must survive it.
1054	
1055	So `postal_reachable` is stored and reported as its own figure. The database
1056	refuses `counts_strict` or `counts_profile_assisted` on a postal row, so the
1057	separation is enforced rather than remembered. Every report gives the three
1058	metrics separately plus a breakdown by route type, and never a single blended
1059	"reachable" number -- which would raise the headline by changing what the
1060	headline means, the exact label inflation Correction 4 was about.
1061	
1062	**ADR-11 · Reachability is reported as two metrics and they are never merged.**
1063	Assumption A1 — that a verified personal profile is a contact route — is a
1064	judgement the brief does not settle, and the reachability count swings from ~60 to
1065	~160 depending on it. Merging them into one number would force a reviewer to
1066	accept our reading of A1 in order to check our arithmetic, which is the same
1067	category of error as Stage 1's single `verified` status: one word standing in for
1068	several different states. `strict_reachable` and `profile_assisted_reachable` are
1069	therefore separate columns, separate metrics, and separate sentences everywhere
1070	they appear. *Cost:* every surface that reports reachability reports two numbers,
1071	which is slightly more to explain. Accepted — the alternative is a headline count
1072	that cannot survive a reviewer disagreeing with one assumption.
1073	
1074	**ADR-10 · Interface copy is validated data.**
1075	Correction 8 holds user-visible sentences to the data truth standard. *Cost:* a
1076	precondition registry every string must join.
1077	
1078	---
1079	
1080	## 15. Pre-build decisions
1081	
1082	Five decisions must be settled before the collect module is written, because each
1083	one changes what we build rather than how well we build it.
1084	
1085	### D1 · Reachability feasibility spike — **run this first**
1086	
1087	200 of 500 must reach a named individual. Stage 1 produced roughly one. This is
1088	the single requirement most likely to fail the stage, and no amount of validation
1089	architecture solves it: validation rejects, it cannot create.
1090	
1091	**Spike design.** 60 candidate firms, stratified 10 per channel, drawn from the
1092	existing Stage 1 candidate pools so no new discovery is needed.
1093	
1094	| Channel | What it might yield | Known risk |
1095	|---|---|---|
1096	| SEC 13F signature block | signatory name, title, phone from a statutory filing | the phone is a filing contact number and may be a **switchboard**, which the corrected standard explicitly excludes |
1097	| SEC ADV Schedule A | named direct owners and executive officers | coverage limited to registered advisers, which most SFOs are not |
1098	| Firm leadership page | named people, sometimes role-specific email | most SFOs have no site; Stage 1 found 14 of 50 |
1099	| Verified principal profile | LinkedIn `/in/` page | proving the profile *belongs* to the named person is the hard part, not finding it |
1100	| Regulatory filing signatories | 13D/G and Form D signature pages | sparse, but statutory |
1101	| Conference speaker profile | name, title, org, occasionally direct contact | recency is good; ownership proof is weak |
1102	
1103	**Metrics collected per channel**, fixed before we start so the comparison is
1104	honest:
1105	
1106	1. `candidates_attempted`
1107	2. `person_identified` — a named human tied to the firm
1108	3. `route_found` — any contact value at all
1109	4. `ownership_evidenced` — evidence that the route reaches *that person*, not the firm
1110	5. `passes_gate_5` — survives the contact-ownership gate
1111	6. `cost_per_qualified` — API calls + wall time per record that reaches (5)
1112	7. `source_concentration_delta` — how far this channel pushes the file toward one source class
1113	
1114	**Decision rule.** Extrapolate (5) to 500 records. If no combination of channels
1115	projects ≥200, we do not proceed to build and instead revisit whether the target
1116	is reachable at all — and say so in the submission rather than shipping 120 and
1117	hoping. A projected shortfall found on day 1 is a design input; found on day 4 it
1118	is a failure.
1119	
1120	**FROZEN 30 Jul — measured, see `SPIKE_REACHABILITY.md`.**
1121	
1122	My prior was that the SEC signatory phone would be a switchboard and fail
1123	ownership. Measurement contradicted it: 6,940 of 9,874 routes adjudicate to an
1124	individual. The channel's limit is reach, not ownership — 50% coverage of
1125	SEC-derived firms, 0% of UK registry and web-derived firms.
1126	
1127	| Channel | Gate-5 yield | Role in the build |
1128	|---|---|---|
1129	| SEC 13F signatory | 50% of SEC-derived firms | primary reachability |
1130	| Verified principal profile | 20% overall, ~2 API calls | primary reachability |
1131	| SEC ADV Schedule A | **0 — structural**, the form has no individual contact field | identity and decision-maker evidence only |
1132	| Companies House | 0% | identity, control evidence, breadth |
1133	| Firm leadership page | 0 of 26 | not pursued |
1134	
1135	**Position on the 200: marginal, not demonstrated.** ~160 projected under
1136	assumption A1 (a verified personal profile counts as a route); ~60 without it.
1137

## 3. Contract integrity — all invariants hold

Run against live data. Every one must be zero.

| Invariant | Result |
|---|---|
| PTC-1 · released claim with no `release_decision` row | **0** |
| PTC-10 · establishing evidence from a foreign extraction event | **0** |
| claims with no establishing evidence | **0** |
| contacts counting toward reachability without ownership evidence | **0** |
| released claims where `attribution` did not pass | **0** |

That last row is the one worth dwelling on. **1,307 claims are released and not
one** reached that state without the attribution gate explicitly passing. In
Stage 1, 93 of 155 quote-backed values were mis-wired. The defect class is now
structurally absent rather than merely unobserved.

### PTC-2, demonstrated and then discharged

Before the fix, 49 SEC `country` claims sat in `candidate`. Their evidence cited a
filing accession number, which the attribution gate classifies as *pointer*
evidence; pointer resolution is Band B and not built, so the gate returned
`skipped` and the release gate treated skipped as not-proven and **held** them.

That is the contract working as specified — an unchecked value did not reach a
customer wearing the appearance of a checked one. It was also the direct cause of
Blocker 1, and it is why the fix changed the *kind* of evidence rather than
loosening the gate. Held claims are now 0.

## 4. Operational behaviour

**Workflows.** Three, all `state=active` on default branch `main`, public repo,
valid cron. `discover` 02/08/14/20 UTC, `refresh` 05/17 UTC, `contract` on
`workflow_run` completion of either.

**Chaining proven.** GitHub's API records the `contract` run as
`event=workflow_run` — nothing human started it. The upstream `discover` shows
`event=workflow_dispatch`.

**Checkpoints advance and resume.** Three rows, keyed `(job, source_id)`:

| job | source | cursor | units |
|---|---|---|---|
| discover | companies_house | 13916919 | 60 |
| discover | sec_13f | name:ONEASCENT FAMILY OFFICE | 8 |
| refresh | companies_house | 13692510 | 40 |

Resume verified three times, including under real failure. The Companies House
cursor was written by the GitHub-hosted run, not locally. The `refresh` cursor was
written by the **scheduled** run. And when the SEC re-derivation was killed by a
10-minute command timeout at unit 41 of 49, the next invocation resumed at
`0001345471` and completed the remaining 8 units with no reprocessing and no
duplicates — the checkpoint doing exactly the job it exists for, against an
unplanned kill rather than a rehearsed one.

**Idempotency.** Deterministic entity ids; a content-hash short circuit that
writes nothing when a source is unchanged (observed: 9 of 9 unchanged on the
refresh run); checkpoints written only after the unit's writes commit.

**Logging.** Structured JSON to stdout (Actions log) and to `s2_run_log` in Neon,
because Actions logs expire and are not queryable. 176 rows across 12 runs, plus
124 rows in `s2_decision_log` (`classify` 118, `budget_halt` 3, `quarantine` 3).

**`/operations`** renders runs, gate outcomes, decisions, refused values and both
reachability metrics, all matching the database.

## 5. Blockers — both resolved

Only two were ever found. Everything else above is either met or later-phase work.

### Blocker 1 — RESOLVED 30 Jul 19:30 UTC

**Was:** zero records both qualifying and reachable. **Now: 39.**

| source | entities | qualifying | reachable | **both** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| companies_house | 69 | 65 | 0 | **0** |
| sec_13f | 49 | 46 | 40 | **39** |

Fixed inside the existing SEC extractor using `COVERPAGE.tsv` fields that were
already loaded — `FILINGMANAGER_STREET1`, `CITY`, `STATEORCOUNTRY`, `ZIPCODE`. No
new source, collector, architecture or policy.

The substantive change was to the *kind* of evidence, not the value. `country`
had been asserted from "Form 13F implies a US manager", citing the accession
number — pointer evidence, which gate 2 correctly deferred and the release gate
correctly held. Now the state code is read from the filing and the country is
re-derived from it by the already-registered `us_state_to_country` rule, so the
gate can check the claim instead of deferring it. All 49 previously-held claims
are now released, each with a detail line of the form *re-derived "United States"
from a two-letter US state code "NY" present in the span*.

The SEC entities were **re-derived, not patched** — their claims were dropped and
rebuilt from the observations, per the roadmap's rule for re-qualification.

**One entity is reachable but still withheld, correctly.** Long Focus Capital
Management files from San Juan, `PR`. The registered rule covers 50 states and
DC, so it returned null and the extractor declined to claim a country rather than
guess one. Whether US territories should map to "United States" is a policy
question, and policy was frozen. One-line fix available if wanted.

## 6. Not blockers, but known and deliberate

- **`value_type` skips 761 of 1,123 claims.** Everything typed `string` has no
  registered checker, so `postcode`, `city` and date fields are unvalidated. A
  quality gap, not a correctness one — no false claim is produced, but a
  malformed one would not be caught.
- **`identity` skipped 1,123/1,123.** No profile claims exist yet; the gate has
  nothing to judge. It is proven against Stage 1's two wrong-person profiles in
  the test suite.
- **`contract` evaluates 0 claims** until `POLICY_VERSION` changes, by design. Its
  PTC-1 audit still runs every execution and fails the job on violation.
- **A `workflow_run`-triggered `contract` records as `trigger='manual'`,**
  understating unattended operation. It does not affect the window, which is
  measured from `discover`/`refresh`, and both record correctly.
- **The 13F dataset is a committed quarterly snapshot** (`data/sec/`, 2.9 MB).
  It will not pick up new filings until refreshed. Stated rather than implied.
- **A run killed by a command timeout left its row in `running`** during the
  re-derivation. `withRun` closes rows on normal failure but cannot on SIGKILL.
  It was closed as `aborted` with the reason recorded. Worth knowing because an
  Actions timeout would do the same, and a row stuck in `running` makes window
  queries ambiguous.
- **Puerto Rico is not in the derivation table**, so one reachable filer stays
  withheld. Correct refusal rather than a guess; see Blocker 1.

## The 500 requirement is unmet — measured, not estimated

**Frozen dataset:** 242 entities · **218 qualifying** · 67 strict reachable ·
174 profile-assisted · 47 postal · **187 with any defensible named-individual
route**.

The 500-record minimum is **not met**. This is a measured ceiling from every
channel built and every channel tested, not a shortfall of effort or runtime.
The qualification standard was never lowered to close it.

### Source ceilings, each measured

| channel | ceiling | how it was measured |
|---|---|---|
| Companies House | **exhausted** | narrow search returned 109 unique companies, **72% already held**, 31 new, 16 rejected as shells (never-filed, dormant, micro-entity), **15 net-new kept** |
| SEC 13F signatory | **56 filers** | full 2025Q3 census: 9,874 routes, 6,948 individually-owned across 6,944 filers, of which **exactly 56** carry `FAMILY`/`FAMILIES` in the registered name |
| SEC Form ADV | **27 net-new** | 942,258 filing rows scanned; 78 family-office-named registrants, 49 filed 2023+, **22 already held** via 13F |
| Verified profiles | **adds routes, not records** | 67% measured on a 30-entity sample; 107 routes created, zero new entities |
| Web discovery | **rejected at ~2–4% precision** | see below |
| **total measured ceiling** | **≈ 240** | against a requirement of 500 |

### The rejected web-discovery spike

40 Serper queries across the four exact phrases, 153 unique candidate domains, 45
fetched for first-party verification. 12 passed the automated filter (27%);
**1–2 were actually family offices**. True precision **~2–4%**.

What the filter let through: `privatebank.jpmorgan.com` and `bbh.com` (banks),
`daypitney.com` and `pillsburylaw.com` (law firms), `kaufmanrossin.com`
(accountancy), `sage.com` (accounting software), `kellogg.northwestern.edu` (a
university), `cowenpartners.com` (executive search), `uhnwinstitute.org` (a trade
body). Extracted "principals" were page furniture: *"Insights Reports Family"*,
*"Enterprise Value"*, *"Chief Investment Officer"*.

**The structural reason:** a single family office has no commercial reason to
publish a website. It serves one family and seeks no clients. The organisations
that rank for `"family office"` are precisely those *selling services to* family
offices, and no wording test separates "we are a family office" from "we advise
family offices".

Importing at that precision would have added ~150 records by placing banks and
law firms in a family-office dataset. The same call was made earlier against the
`family wealth` search terms, which returned independent financial advisers
(`IFS FAMILY WEALTH ADVISERS`, `REDWOOD FINANCIAL FAMILY WEALTH & ESTATE
PLANNERS`), and in Phase 0 against the leadership-page probe, which measured 0
of 26.

**Reproduce:** `WEB_QUERIES=40 WEB_FETCH=45 npx tsx packages/pipeline/src/discovery/sample-web.ts`

### The position, stated plainly

The brief says a submission below 500 fails, and also that a file containing
values labelled more strongly than the evidence supports cannot be trusted. Both
could not be satisfied from the sources available. **218 records that hold, with
the ceiling measurements attached, was chosen over 500 that do not.**

# Postscript — the 500 requirement, and how this section became wrong

Everything above this line was written when the file held 218 qualifying records
and I believed that was a measured ceiling. It is preserved unedited because it
was an honest reading of the evidence at the time and the correction is more
useful than a tidy document.

**The ceiling was a bug, not a limit.** Two defects in discovery, and the second
was the expensive one. Searches asked for `size=40` and never read the `hits`
total or used `start_index`, so a term with 286 matches returned 40. And the SIC
filter was an assumption about which codes family offices register under, not an
inclusion standard: `"family office"` filtered to SIC 64205 returns 11 hits;
unfiltered it returns 286. The firms behind that filter register under 68209,
70221, 68320 — whatever their accountant chose.

Fixing both took the qualifying count from 218 to 614 without relaxing a single
gate, the shell filter, the ownership adjudication or the commercial floor.

**Then two risk reviews took it back down.** The first, of the 27
records whose names suggested a service provider withheld ten: two insurers, two
family law firms, a tax practice, an IFA, two grantmaking foundations and a
consultancy. Seventeen ambiguous advisers and multi-family offices were retained
with their status unresolved, because the brief requires that ambiguity stay
visible rather than be cleaned away. That left 603.

**The second review, prompted by an external audit, found the deeper problem.**
The commercial floor asked whether a record was complete and never whether the
firm was a family office, so a bakery, a funeral home, a golf club, a
rail-supplies company, two acquisition shells and eleven hedge funds had
qualified on an address and a director alone — 54% of the file carried no
classification at all. Qualification now requires affirmative evidence at one of
three stated tiers and a named individual is mandatory. That cut the file to 554,
and further collection under the tightened standard brought it to **581**.

**Final state, reconciled across every surface:**

| | |
|---|---|
| active unmerged entities | 740 |
| qualifying | **581** |
| strict reachable | 54 |
| profile-assisted reachable | **388** |
| postal reachable | 87 |
| any defensible route | 420 |
| unassessed | 0 |

`packages/pipeline/src/jobs/reconcile.ts` checks these across the database, both
exports and the live product, and exits non-zero on any disagreement.

**Postal fell from 207 to 93, and to 87 in the final file,** after an audit found the registered-office test
compared addresses as exact strings, so the same building filed two ways passed
it. 130 routes were cleared, kept in the file with `counts_postal` false and a
decision-log entry naming both addresses.

**The scheduled staleness condition is now met.** A scheduled `discover` run on
3 August detected **7 evidence-based staleness events**, each a content-hash
change against a reading from an earlier cycle. Traced end to end: company
`09984032` was read on 1 Aug at 17:00Z with hash `ab7028962d6` and re-read by the
scheduled run on 3 Aug at 21:50Z with hash `b78d0c8d672`. Two days apart, content
compared rather than a clock consulted. **All three operating-window conditions
are satisfied.**

**Still unmet: ≥200 reachable on the strict metric.** Stage 1 defined a confirmed
contact route as a direct phone or verified email — its own submission reports
"10 of 50 for direct phone lines and 4 for email" and holds a postal address
separately as "a slower contact route". By that definition the count is **54**.
Every source was tested: SEC 13F signature blocks are the only one publishing
personal phone numbers and were exhausted across four quarters; SEC ADV, the IAPD
API and Companies House publish none; Hunter's free tier resets after the
submission deadline. Stated plainly rather than met by relabelling a weaker
metric.
